name: Sanbor Medical Corporation
old_description: We help medical device OEMs reduce manufacturing costs by 20-25%.
about:
Sanbor Medical Corporation, headquartered in Allentown, Pennsylvania, has over 30 years of production experience in medical device contract manufacturing. The privately held company operates manufacturing facilities in Allentown; Xiamen, China; and Penang, Malaysia, along with a European office in the Netherlands and a distribution center in Los Angeles, California.

The company provides turnkey contract manufacturing for Class I and II finished medical devices and Class I, II, and III subassemblies. Its capabilities include cleanroom assembly, PCB assembly with ESD-compliant storage, testing, programming and validation, packaging and labeling, and global supply chain management. Sanbor handles multi-volume production, product line transfers, and new product introduction across its global footprint.

Sanbor serves medical device OEMs ranging from startups to several top-30 global medical device companies. Its customer base includes well-established firms and emerging ventures seeking cost-effective, compliant manufacturing solutions.

Sanbor differentiates itself through a global manufacturing footprint that enables cost reductions of 20–25%, a quality system that has passed FDA audits with zero non-conformities, and rigorous audits by medical device OEMs. The company emphasizes documentation, compliance, and risk management across all facilities.

name: Sanchelima International
old_description: Founded in 1980, we focus on providing ideal technical solutions for processors in the food and dairy industries.
about:
Sanchelima International is based in Doral, Florida, and was founded in 1980. The company began as a provider of technical solutions for processors in the food and dairy industries.

The company supplies a range of industrial equipment for dairy processing, including HTST and tubular pasteurizers, homogenizers, high‑pressure pumps, centrifugal and cream separators, cheesemaking vats, molders and presses, whey‑processing membrane systems, evaporators and spray dryers, vertical/horizontal/thermoforming packaging machines, automated CIP cleaning systems, butter churns and cutters, and yogurt production modules. It also provides installation, commissioning, preventive maintenance, original spare parts, and technical consulting. Sanchelima serves customers in the United States, Mexico, and Latin America.

Its customers include milk and dairy processing plants, cheese factories producing fresh, aged, and pasta‑filata varieties, yogurt, cream, and butter producers, whey‑processing facilities, and other food operations requiring thermal treatment or automation. The company works with both new‑equipment buyers and those seeking refurbished units for faster deployment.

Sanchelima emphasizes decades of engineering expertise that spans single‑unit sourcing to complete turnkey plant solutions. It differentiates itself by offering both new equipment with full manufacturer warranties and energy‑efficient technology, as well as tested refurbished equipment for lower upfront cost. The firm also highlights immediate delivery from stock for urgent replacements and customized special‑order configurations.

Sanders Metal Products operates from Fargo, North Dakota, where it has provided custom metal fabrication for over 30 years. The company’s founding year and original owners are not disclosed in public materials.

The shop offers a full range of metalworking services: welding, metal fabrication and cutting, CNC machining (including vertical milling and turning), plasma cutting, vertical band sawing, painting and lining, and assembly. Equipment includes a CNC 400-amp HD plasma cutter, a VT 120 HA-50 HE&M high-speed vertical band saw, vertical CNC machining centers, and several CNC lathes (Cincinnati and Clausing 2040 models). Sanders serves customers who need structural metalwork, industrial equipment components, and artistic metal installations—summarized on its site as “structures standing, equipment working, or artwork hanging.” No specific industry sectors or client names are listed.

The company emphasizes its breadth of in-house capabilities and experienced welders and machinists as differentiators, promoting itself as a “custom metal fabrication shop in the Midwest” that handles projects of any scale and welcomes walk-in inquiries.

name: Sandia Mountain Solar
old_description: In New Mexico, Sandia Mountain Solar leads the charge as the area's premier expert in ground-mounted PV solutions. Our team specializes in designing and implementing custom solar power ground-mounted systems that maximize energy output and minimize environmental impact.
about:
Sandia Mountain Solar was established in September 2017 in Sandia Park, New Mexico, as a division of Morgan's Constructive Solutions, LLC, a general construction firm. The solar division emerged from the parent company's construction experience, applying that background to the design and installation of photovoltaic systems.

The company installs roof-mounted, ground-mounted, and carport solar arrays for both grid-tied and off-grid applications. It also provides post-installation system monitoring and assists customers with federal Investment Tax Credit documentation. For qualifying commercial clients, the team helps prepare USDA REAP Grant applications that can cover up to 25 percent of project costs. In addition to solar work, the crew performs general and electrical construction tasks.

Sandia Mountain Solar serves residential homeowners and commercial property owners across central New Mexico, including Sandia Park, Cedar Crest, Moriarty, Tijeras, Algodones, Bernalillo, and Edgewood. Commercial customers include agricultural producers and rural businesses eligible for USDA energy grants. The company also works with property owners who lack utility access or require backup power during grid outages.

The firm says its construction heritage distinguishes it from sales-driven solar providers, allowing it to handle challenging sites and deliver cleaner installations with active monitoring. It emphasizes honest, professional client relationships and partners with module and inverter manufacturers.

name: Santa Fe Hat Company
old_description: Santa Fe Hat Company is a division of Montecristi Custom Hat Works, Santa Fe’s premier custom hat maker for over 50 years.
about:
Santa Fe Hat Company is located in the historic Guadalupe district of Santa Fe, New Mexico. Founded in 1976 by Milton R. Johnson, the business began as a combined retail store and custom hat-making shop. Johnson later acquired a second studio that became Montecristi Custom Hat Works, the company's custom manufacturing division. The company remains at its original Plaza-area location.

The company produces custom hats through Montecristi Custom Hat Works, specializing in handwoven Panama straw hats from Ecuador and beaver fur felt hats sourced from European and U.S. mills. It also operates a retail division carrying brands such as Stetson, Borsalino, Larry Mahan, Serratelli, Fernandez y Roche, and its own SFHC label. In addition, the shop fabricates artisan hat bands using materials including sterling silver, gold, porcupine quill, braided leather, and horsehair.

Santa Fe Hat Company serves individual consumers and wholesale buyers seeking high-quality headwear and custom accessories. Its customer base includes retail shoppers at the Santa Fe storefront and buyers of the SFHC brand and Montecristi custom hats. The company does not specify industrial sectors beyond apparel and fashion accessories.

The founder's guiding principle—“Fashions come and go, but a stylish hat lasts forever”—reflects the company's focus on enduring craftsmanship. The firm distinguishes itself through its half-century heritage, direct access to Ecuadorian Panama weavers, and a curated selection of premium felt and straw hats alongside locally crafted hat bands.

about:
Santa Fe Steel, a structural steel fabricator and retail outlet, operates from Santa Fe, New Mexico. The company was established in 2008 when Charles Quintana, a licensed general contractor with decades of construction experience, teamed up with Chris to address what they saw as a shortage of customer-focused, high-quality steel fabrication in the region. The business is locally owned and operated.

The shop provides full-service structural steel fabrication, including manual plasma cutting, punching (with 30-, 65-, and 90-ton capacity), and multi-process welding in carbon and alloy steels. No facility square footage or employee count is disclosed.

Santa Fe Steel serves commercial, industrial, and residential construction clients across Northern New Mexico, though the company does not publish a detailed industry list. Its retail outlet also supplies steel products directly to walk-in customers.

The founders started the company to bring better service and fabrication quality to the local market. Their stated priority is meeting or exceeding contract requirements, and all welding procedures follow American Welding Society standards.

name: Santee Wire Products Inc
old_description: T.D. Powell started his career at Andrews Wire/Georgetown Steel in 1970. He moved to Beaumont, TX in 1974 where Georgetown Steel built a plant. In 1983 T.D. moved back to South Carolina to venture out on his own. He founded
about:
Santee Wire Products Inc was founded in 1983 by T.D. Powell in Holly Hill, South Carolina. Powell began his career at Andrews Wire/Georgetown Steel in 1970 and later moved to Beaumont, Texas, where Georgetown Steel built a plant. In 1983 he returned to South Carolina to start his own venture, establishing the company with straight and cut machines. The business remains family owned and operated.

The company produces wire products using processes that include wire drawing, straightening, cutting, and annealing. An annealing furnace was installed in 1993 to expand capabilities. Operations are housed in a temperature-controlled warehouse, and the company notes that most items are kept in stock for prompt shipment.

Santee Wire Products serves a range of industries that use wire for springs, bedding, furniture, automotive components, display racks, sod staples, and insulation supports. Customers include manufacturers and fabricators in those sectors.

The company emphasizes its family-owned structure and inventory availability as key differentiators, aiming to provide quick turnaround on standard wire items.

name: Sargent Metal
old_description: We have proudly been blazing new trails in the metal fabrication industry since 1975.
about:
Sargent Metal operates from Anderson, South Carolina, where it was founded in 1975 as a family-owned metal fabrication business. The company has remained under family ownership since its inception, building a reputation for adapting to evolving industry demands.

The shop provides a full range of metal fabrication and finishing services, including CNC fiber laser cutting, CNC punching, deburring and edge rounding, CNC and robotic forming, MIG, TIG, and robotic welding, hardware insertion, powder coating, and value-added assembly. Equipment includes Trumpf laser cutting systems, and the facility handles both manual and robotic welding for materials such as aluminum, cold-rolled steel, HRPO, galvaneal, and stainless steel.

Sargent Metal serves a diverse set of industries: military (ground support systems and missile containers), people movers (elevator and escalator enclosures), power control (switchgear cabinets), safety (EMS and fire vehicle assemblies), transportation (rail and trailer components), vending (kiosks and safes), commercial vehicle (light vehicle, heavy truck, and bus parts), construction (loader, crane, and excavator components), data center (server and network infrastructure enclosures), energy management (HVAC and refrigeration housings), food equipment (oven and fryer assemblies), and HVAC (mechanical system components).

The company attributes its longevity to continuous investment in technological advancement, the ability to adapt to new markets, and an enduring commitment to its team and customers, rooted in its family-owned culture.

about:
Sargento Foods Inc. was founded in 1953 in Plymouth, Wisconsin, as a family-owned cheese company. The business began with a commitment to putting the family name on every slice and shred, a promise that remains central to its identity today.

The company produces a range of natural cheese products including sliced cheese, shredded cheese, snack cheese, snack trays, and block cheese. Its operations focus on transforming dairy into portioned and packaged formats for retail and foodservice channels, though specific facility size and production volumes are not disclosed.

Sargento serves consumers through grocery retailers and foodservice operators, offering products that appear in household kitchens and restaurant menus alike. The brand’s portfolio includes snack kits such as Balanced Breaks and Mighty Bites, which pair cheese with nuts, crackers, or meats.

The company emphasizes its heritage of innovation over more than 70 years, highlighting real, natural cheese as its differentiator. Its founding principle — “A Promise You Can Taste” — underscores a focus on ingredient transparency and consistent quality.

name: Sarica Manufacturing Co
old_description: Three SMT Lines Featuring the Latest MY300 Placement Machines
about:
Sarica Manufacturing Co operates from Urbana, Ohio, as a woman-owned small business (WOSB) providing electronic manufacturing services. The company serves commercial aerospace, Department of Defense, and medical markets with a global footprint spanning North America, Europe, and the Middle East.

The company runs three surface-mount technology lines equipped with MY300 placement machines, supporting through-hole assembly, wire bonding, and full box-build integration. Core outputs include circuit card assemblies, cable assemblies, and wire harnesses, each verified through a first-article inspection process on initial shipments. Engineering support covers design consultation and quick-turn revisions to move programs from development to full-rate production.

Customers span aerospace, defense, medical, industrial, and automotive sectors. Sarica works with prime contractors and OEMs needing flexible capacity—whether a single process step or turn-key electro-mechanical assembly—to meet design-to-cost targets and schedule volatility on new development programs.

A flat organizational structure and a stated sense of urgency allow real-time design changes and rapid response to shifting requirements. The firm emphasizes a lower cost structure without sacrificing quality or on-time delivery, positioning itself as a partner for capacity-constrained organizations seeking to offload non-core assembly work.
